definition: Cannabis abuse is problematic use of cannabis that is serious enough to be identified as a clinically relevant substance-use problem. In this source, it is discussed alongside cannabis dependence and measured as risk or severity scores rather than described in detail.

reasons: The definition adds an unsupported clinical gloss: the source only refers to “cannabis abuse/dependence (CAST/SDS) scores” and does not define cannabis abuse as a clinically relevant substance-use problem.
The source presents cannabis abuse/dependence as a measured score in a study, not as a detailed conceptual definition, so the definitional claim goes beyond the packet.

The packet does not define what “cannabis abuse” means (e.g., “problematic use” or “serious enough to be identified…”); it only refers to “cannabis abuse/dependence” as variables measured by CAST/SDS.

The packet supports that cannabis abuse/dependence is discussed alongside dependence and analyzed via CAST/SDS scores, but it does not support the specific characterization that it is “measured as risk or severity scores rather than described in detail” (the text does not call them “severity” scores, nor does it explicitly contrast measurement vs. description in the way the definition states).
